steps.say: Living donors are staged giving one kidney safely. Laparoscopic donor nephrectomy is performed routinely. The left kidney is picked for its longer vein. The short right vein is staged draining directly into vena cava. Longer veins are staged easing the recipient join. Donor safety is staged outranking all convenience.
steps.tx: **Donor nephrectomy** (living kidney harvest), usually laparoscopic, takes the left kidney for its **longer left renal vein** (roomy outflow channel), since the short right vein drains directly into the IVC. Spare adrenal with gonadal branches on the left. Prioritize donor safety over recipient ease, because donors must leave whole.

steps.say: The new kidney is staged sitting low in the belly. Heterotopic placement is staged putting the graft in the iliac fossa. The pocket is opened extraperitoneally on one side. The renal artery is sewn joining external or internal iliac vessels. The vein is staged meeting the external iliac vein. Native kidneys are left untouched behind.
steps.tx: **Heterotopic placement** (new kidney low site) seats the allograft in the **iliac fossa** (groin pocket) extraperitoneally with **external iliac anastomosis** (groin vessel joins) of artery to external or internal iliac vessels. Leave native kidneys behind untouched. Close over drains with reperfusion watched, because twists declare themselves early.

vis.caption: Heterotopic graft: iliac fossa pocket with iliac joins. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: The new ureter is staged needing a safe bladder join. Extravesical Lich Gregoir reimplantation is staged as standard. A submucosal tunnel is staged resisting reflux naturally. A double J stent is staged splinting the join routinely. Leak with obstruction rates are staged staying lowest this way. Stents are removed cystoscopically in weeks.
steps.tx: **Lich-Gregoir allograft reimplantation** (outside bladder join) builds an extravesical tunnel with a **double-J stent** (internal splint) for the lowest leak and obstruction rates. Stent routinely and remove cystoscopically in weeks. Watch drainage volumes after removal, because strictures declare then with rising creatinine.

steps.say: Ureter narrowing is staged following poor blood supply here. Distal ischaemia is staged starving the lower ureter. Harvest devascularizes the donor lower pole segment. Stenosis rates of two to five percent are quoted. Rising creatinine with hydronephrosis is staged warning early. Stenting with reconstruction is staged rescuing most cases.
steps.tx: **Transplant ureteral stenosis** (graft tube narrowing) in **2% to 5%** (two to five in a hundred) follows distal **ureteral ischemia** (lower tube blood loss) from lower pole devascularization at harvest. Suspect with rising creatinine and hydronephrosis. Stent first and reconstruct failures, because late grafts tolerate little.

steps.say: Early leaks are staged threatening graft and patient. Rising creatinine with pelvic pain is staged warning loudly. Wound drainage is tested for creatinine content. Drain fluid far above serum is staged proving a leak. Stenting with repair is staged sealing most defects. Large necrotic ends are staged needing reimplantation.
steps.tx: **Transplant urine leak** (anastomosis drip) in **1% to 4%** (one to four in a hundred) shows rising creatinine with pelvic pain and wound drainage, where **drain fluid creatinine** (wound water kidney value) far above serum proves the leak. Stent small defects and reimplant necrotic ends. Drain collections widely, because urine invites infection.

steps.say: Lymph collections are staged squeezing the graft silently always. Unligated iliac lymphatics are staged leaking after dissection. Lymphocele rates of one to fifteen percent are quoted. Vein or ureter compression is staged declaring the symptomatic ones. Fenestration into the peritoneum is staged draining them durably. Marsupialization is performed laparoscopically.
steps.tx: **Lymphocele** (lymph collection) in **1% to 15%** (one to fifteen in a hundred) follows unligated recipient iliac lymphatics, compressing graft vein or ureter when symptomatic. Treat by laparoscopic **peritoneal fenestration** (window opening), **marsupialization** (pouch drainage), for lasting drainage. Ligate lymphatics routinely at implant, because prevention beats reoperation.

steps.say: Late hypertension is staged signalling inflow disease early. Refractory pressure with graft dysfunction is staged warning loudly. Transplant artery stenosis is staged narrowing the join. Duplex with angiography is staged confirming the lesion. Angioplasty with stenting is staged opening most narrowings. Pressure with creatinine is staged settling after success.
steps.tx: **Transplant renal artery stenosis** (join narrowing) presents with refractory hypertension and graft dysfunction, fixed by percutaneous **angioplasty and stenting** (balloon plus scaffold). Confirm with duplex then angiography. Recheck pressure with creatinine after success, because restenosis returns silently without watch. Repeat duplex surveillance follows every intervention.

vis.caption: Artery stenosis: angioplasty with stenting restores inflow. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Sudden shutdown in days is staged threatening the graft. Vein thrombosis is staged striking under one to two percent. The first forty eight to seventy two hours are staged carrying the risk. Oliguria with severe swelling is staged alarming the ward. Graft loss is staged following missed cases rapidly. Exploration with thrombectomy is booked emergently.
steps.tx: **Renal vein thrombosis** (catastrophic graft clot) under **1% to 2%** (under one to two in a hundred) hits within **48 to 72 hours** (forty eight to seventy two hours) with severe **graft swelling** (bloated graft), sudden pain, and rapid **oliguria** (no urine) to graft loss. Explore emergently with thrombectomy on suspicion. Never watch a swelling graft, because minutes decide salvage.
